10 seconds anime fight scene: wizard versus acrobat in a moonlit bamboo courtyard

Choreography: every effect follows its cause along the causal links; final instruction: end on A spiral sweep windup, B crouched guard landing.
Euler degrees XYZ.
Render spec exactly.

[MOVEMENT LANGUAGE]
Labanotation written as words. Mode: Euler-heavy: every line carries Root, EulerXYZ and the full Joints dictionary; the staff words stay primary.
Each line = one measure for one performer; time in seconds; a symbol lasts until the next line.
SUPPORT names what bears the weight; NO SUPPORT = airborne.
Contact bow = touch; [contact: X-Y retained] = held; [contact: Y ENDS – released] = let go; DOUBLE BOW + accent = a strike (interp.: a momentary contact with a strong accent).
Directions are relative to the performer's front: forward, back, left, right and the diagonals between them; levels high, mid, low; place-high / place-low = straight up / down. A limb reads mid while within 45 degrees of horizontal (interp.). Lower arm and lower leg: straight, or folded by degrees.
Turns name the axis and the plane: a flip turns about the side-to-side axis (sagittal plane), a spin about the vertical axis (transverse plane), a cartwheel about the front-to-back axis (frontal plane); each turn is written once, on the line where it starts, with its count.

Explicit = the written lines (every support change, contact and accent has one); implied = everything between lines.
Root [x, y, z] is the scene position in metres; EulerXYZ and joints are degrees.
